The obligation 'while holding the key, the door must be open then or opened later' is correctly operationalized: u1 is the pending-duty state, and key_lost in u1 is an explicit regression to u0 with -0.2, matching the domain's framing of key_lost as losing the key before the door opens; since door_open is impossible without has_door_key, resetting to u0 is behaviorally equivalent to a dedicated pending-duty state, and recovery (re-pick, then open) remains possible, consistent with 'opened later'. key_lost in u2 is correctly absorbed by the else self-loop: once the door has been opened, a later drop (even with the door toggled shut) does not violate the obligation, so regressing there would punish compliant behavior. Events vs conditions: key_lost (event) is used only as a one-shot edge trigger; persistent conditions drive level edges, and the pickup+toggle step loses nothing because door_open persists into the next valuation. Reward safety: progress rewards 0.1/0.2/1.0 are bounded and increasing toward the goal; the only repeatable cycle (u1 -(key_lost)-> u0 -(has_door_key)-> u1) nets -0.1, and the door_open and target_picked_up rewards cannot be re-earned since u2 has no edge back to u1, so there is no reward exploit.
